message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"7.11","text":"If I were able to cause earthquakes and to do anything at all I wish, I am not saying that I would annihilate Simon together with his companions—for I have not been sent to bring destruction on human beings—but I would make him my friend, so that, by slandering my true proclamation, he might not hinder many on their way to salvation. But if you believe me, he himself is a magician, he himself a slanderer, he himself a servant of evil against those who do not know the truth. And for this reason he can produce diseases in those who sin, having those who sin as partners in the power directed against them. But I am a servant of God, who made all things, and a disciple of his right-side prophet. Therefore, as that prophet’s apostle, I speak the truth. For in serving what is good, I also drive diseases away. For I was sent second, since disease goes first and healing follows. Thus, through that magician who does evil, having disbelieved God, you became ill; but through me, if you believe him, you will be healed. For in this way, having experienced power and turned to doing good, you might also be able to save your souls.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"Σίμωνα οὐ λέγω ὅτι μετὰ τῶν αὐτοῦ ἑταίρων ἐξωλόθρευον","chosen":"I am not saying that I would annihilate Simon together with his companions","rationale":"The imperfect ἐξωλόθρευον functions as the unreal result of the preceding condition; “annihilate” preserves its intensive destructive force."},{"source_quote":"αὐτὸς διάβολος","chosen":"he himself a slanderer","rationale":"διάβολος can mean “slanderer” or “devil.” The nearby cognate διαβάλλων (“slandering”) supports the common-noun sense, while “he himself a devil” remains a viable alternative."},{"source_quote":"ἁμαρτάνουσι νόσους ἐνεργεῖν δύναται","chosen":"he can produce diseases in those who sin","rationale":"ἁμαρτάνουσι is taken as a dative plural participle, anticipated by τοὺς ἁμαρτάνοντας. Morphologically it could instead be finite—“they sin”—with a sentence break after it."},{"source_quote":"συνεργοὺς ἔχων τοὺς ἁμαρτάνοντας τῆς κατ’ αὐτῶν δυνάμεως","chosen":"having those who sin as partners in the power directed against them","rationale":"The sinners paradoxically cooperate in the power exercised against them; the rendering preserves both the partnership and the hostile direction of the power."},{"source_quote":"τοῦ δεξιοῦ αὐτοῦ προφήτου μαθητής","chosen":"a disciple of his right-side prophet","rationale":"δεξιοῦ modifies “prophet” and marks him as right or right-sided. “Right-hand prophet” is possible, but may suggest merely a trusted assistant; replacing it with “true prophet” would erase the printed wording."},{"source_quote":"ἐκείνου ἀπόστολος ὢν","chosen":"as that prophet’s apostle","rationale":"ἐκείνου most naturally refers to the immediately preceding prophet. Reference to God is grammatically possible but less immediate."},{"source_quote":"ἀγαθῷ γὰρ ὑπηρετῶν","chosen":"For in serving what is good","rationale":"The substantival ἀγαθῷ may denote goodness or a good person, including “the Good One.” The neutral wording preserves the contrast with serving evil without fixing the referent."},{"source_quote":"ἐπέμφθην γὰρ δεύτερος","chosen":"For I was sent second","rationale":"δεύτερος indicates his position in the sequence subsequently explained: disease precedes and healing follows."},{"source_quote":"ἐάν τε αὐτῷ πιστεύσητε","chosen":"if you believe him","rationale":"The pronoun is retained in English. God is the most likely antecedent because this belief contrasts with τῷ θεῷ ἀπιστήσαντες, though the magician is grammatically nearer."},{"source_quote":"τοῦ δυνατοῦ τὴν πεῖραν λαβόντες","chosen":"having experienced power","rationale":"The substantival δυνατοῦ can denote power or “the Powerful One.” The main rendering leaves the possessor unstated, as does the Greek, while the latter personal interpretation remains possible."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ἐάν τε αὐτῷ πιστεύσητε","issue":"The postpositive τε has no explicit correlative in the printed construction. It can be read as a weak connective whose force is absorbed into the coordinated contrast, so no correction is required.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"7.12","text":"As he was saying these things, they all lay kneeling at his feet. He, however, raised his hands toward heaven, prayed to God, and healed them all by prayer alone. After remaining with the people of Beirut for quite a few days, accustoming many to monarchical worship and baptizing them, and appointing as their bishop one of the elders who followed him, he departed for Byblos. When he arrived there and learned that Simon had not stayed with them for even one day but had immediately hurried to Tripolis, he stayed with them for a few days, healed quite a few people, and trained them in the books; then he traveled to Tripolis in Simon’s tracks, having chosen to pursue him rather than flee from him.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"γονυπετεῖς πρὸ τῶν αὐτοῦ ἔκειντο ποδῶν","chosen":"they all lay kneeling at his feet","rationale":"The wording preserves both ἔκειντο, “lay,” and γονυπετεῖς, “kneeling” or “fallen on the knees.”"},{"source_quote":"τῇ μοναρχικῇ θρησκείᾳ συνεθίσας","chosen":"accustoming many to monarchical worship","rationale":"θρησκεία can mean worship, religious observance, or religion, while μοναρχική evokes sole rule or sovereignty. “The religion of sole rule” is a possible more literal alternative."},{"source_quote":"ἕνα ἐπίσκοπον αὐτοῖς καταστήσας","chosen":"appointing as their bishop one","rationale":"ἐπίσκοπος literally denotes an overseer, but “bishop” fits the explicitly appointed community office in this historical narrative."},{"source_quote":"τοῖς Βηρυτίοις","chosen":"with the people of Beirut","rationale":"The Greek uses the civic demonym rather than the city name; the rendering makes that reference explicit in conventional English."},{"source_quote":"ταῖς βίβλοις αὐτοὺς ἐνασκήσας","chosen":"trained them in the books","rationale":"The definite plural βίβλοις is retained as “the books”; the source does not explicitly identify them as Scripture."},{"source_quote":"κατ’ ἴχνος τοῦ Σίμωνος","chosen":"in Simon’s tracks","rationale":"This preserves the source’s physical trail or footprint image rather than reducing it to the abstract “after Simon.”"},{"source_quote":"μεταδιώκειν αὐτὸν μᾶλλον, οὐχ ὑποφεύγειν","chosen":"to pursue him rather than flee from him","rationale":"The contrast is between continuing the pursuit and withdrawing or slipping away; “flee from him” gives the natural English opposition."}],"source_issues":[]}]}
